extraction.Name: Laura Patton—nee Merrival
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to her allotment of 152.88 acres, when it was issued, April 13, 1918, for the reason that she did not want to pay taxes; but the Indian Agency advised her that, if she did not take charge of it, the land would be taxed just the same, and finally be sold for taxes, so she took the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold her allotment, in 1920, to Harry Evans, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for the sum of $1600.00, cash
extraction.Buyer: Harry Evans, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for the sum of $1600.00, cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: at that time, she paid up her back taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: she and her children are supported by her husband, who is a United States mail carrier, and also handles a freight line, for his living; and that this is the source of his income
extraction.NOTES: has very poor health; has 7 minor children, all in good health; did not sell her allotment for debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee; considers she received a fair price for her land; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document number No. 51; County of Shannon, State of South Dakota; subscribed and sworn before Notary Public on December 20, 1928 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 49 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
